Their much larger single-path steps favor measurement excursions over joint pressure events. Exact excursion seconds and simultaneous partner pressures are unavailable; these recording-wide comparisons do not confirm a hardware cause.

Operating and other pressure changes
P7's supported problem is gateway-P7-0, the shared measurement connection affecting both A/B taps at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7. During 90-105 seconds, P7-ST1-A/B shifted -0.787/-0.777 bar from their first-60-second references, while P7-ST2-A/B on another connection shifted only -0.033/-0.030 bar. During 105-120 seconds these were -0.773/-0.789 versus -0.021/-0.003 bar. The approximately 0.75-bar displacement starts in the calibration period beginning at 90 seconds and matches the recorded approximately -0.75-bar conversion offset. The every-other-station footprint fits one shared-path problem better than a localized leak; eight affected taps are not independent witnesses.

P2's positive transition matches the operating record's expected approximately +0.4 bar during 90-145 seconds. P2-ST1-A/B rose +0.353/+0.372 bar during 90-105 seconds and +0.356/+0.354 bar during 105-120 seconds relative to their early references. P2-ST8-A/B rose less: +0.267/+0.275 and +0.216/+0.234 bar in those periods. Sign and observed timing match, with a smaller magnitude farther along the pipe; the recording observes only the overlap through 120 seconds. There is no supported joint leak pattern on P2 in this window. P2-ST2-A's separate excursion remains suspect, while P2-ST8-B changes with A and is not demonstrated to be stuck.

P4 has a weaker joint pressure footprint, not an established second leak source. During 115-120 seconds, P4-ST1-A/B were 0.156/0.172 bar below normal, versus P5-ST4-A's 1.327-bar deficit over the same period. During 105-120 seconds, P4-ST1-A/B's early-reference changes were -0.185/-0.188 bar. Their agreement supports a real paired pressure change rather than isolated spikes, but its relationship to P5 remains unresolved: neither hydraulic propagation nor a separate leak is established.

Limits of this result
During 60-120 seconds, P1-ST7-B, P3-ST5-B and P6-ST6-A each had 50/60 usable readings, with 10/60 missing; P4-ST8-A had 52/60 usable readings despite receiving 60, leaving 8/60 unusable. These are unavailable observations, not measured losses or proof of hardware failure. The health review is partial and does not establish that all other instruments are reliable. Independent pressure/flow evidence from the recorded incident period is the physical-confirmation boundary. An independent loss outside P7's shared connection would weaken its calibration-only explanation; independently confirmed deterioration at P5's central focus would strengthen the integrity diagnosis.

competing_causes.text: P5 supports a leak-pattern diagnosis rather than an isolated instrument explanation. During 115-120 seconds, P5-ST4-A/B were 1.327/1.353 bar below the normal reference, compared with neighboring P5-ST3-A/B at 1.005/0.991 bar. During 105-120 seconds, ST4-A/B also agreed on early-reference changes of -1.325/-1.350 bar, while paired ST5 on a different connection changed -1.280/-1.272 bar. Persistence and agreement across connections strengthen the physical-pressure interpretation, but do not identify a confirmed cause. No verified P5 operation is supplied; incomplete logs leave an unrecorded operating cause or broader common bias unexcluded. Independent pressure/flow records covering the observed event could distinguish these alternatives without repeating the available pressure comparisons.

P7 supports a shared-conversion-path explanation: P7-ST1-A/B changed -0.787/-0.777 bar during 90-105 seconds, compared with independent-connection P7-ST2-A/B at -0.033/-0.030 bar. These changes are relative to each sensor's first-60-second typical pressure. The affected pair's roughly 0.75-bar displacement matches the calibration record's approximately -0.75-bar offset beginning at 90 seconds, while the adjacent pair lacks that displacement. Both taps at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 share the affected connection, so their agreement is not independent corroboration of a leak. This connection-level finding can coexist with P5's separate pressure pattern and the isolated suspect instruments. A recorded independent pressure loss outside the affected connection would contradict a calibration-only explanation; the physical conversion fault itself is not confirmed.

P2's pressure rise is supported as an operating transition: P2-ST1-A/B changed +0.353/+0.372 bar during 90-105 seconds, versus -0.029/-0.038 bar during 75-90 seconds, and remained at +0.356/+0.354 bar during 105-120 seconds relative to their first-60-second references. Its positive sign, approximately 0.4-bar magnitude and observed start match the approved 90-145-second pressure-setting record. P2-ST8-A/B rose less, +0.216/+0.234 bar during 105-120 seconds, so the match is not spatially uniform. Separately, during the 0-120-second recording, P2-ST2-A's 2.934-bar largest adjacent step contrasts with P2-ST2-B's 0.298-bar largest step, supporting a suspect excursion rather than the shared operating rise. The positive transition does not explain P5's negative central pattern. No observation beyond 120 seconds is supplied, and temporal agreement does not prove an exclusive cause.

regional_assessments.text: P5's final-five-second deficits during 115-120 seconds were ST3-A/B 1.005/0.991 bar, ST4-A/B 1.327/1.353 bar, ST5-A/B 1.319/1.297 bar and ST6-A/B 0.922/0.917 bar below the supplied normal reference. All eight instruments had five usable readings in that period; paired agreement and the stronger contiguous ST4-ST5 focus support a joint pressure-loss pattern across both measurement connections. Evolution also agrees: during 90-105 seconds ST4-A/B changed -0.920/-0.886 bar and ST5-A/B -0.939/-0.828 bar, deepening during 105-120 seconds to -1.325/-1.350 and -1.280/-1.272 bar relative to their first-60-second references. The accepted midpoint rule bounds the central 700/900-m stations against their weaker 500/1100-m neighbors at 600-1000 m. This pressure-focus heuristic supports inspection priority, not a physical leak point; incomplete operating coverage and unexcluded broader common causes limit causal certainty. Independent pressure/flow evidence from the recorded event would discriminate a physical loss from a shared bias.

The affected footprint is both A/B taps at P7-ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 on gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection. During 90-105 seconds their first-60-second-reference changes were respectively -0.787/-0.777, -0.778/-0.771, -0.783/-0.777 and -0.765/-0.798 bar; independent-connection P7-ST2-A/B changed only -0.033/-0.030 bar. During 105-120 seconds the affected pairs remained displaced by -0.773/-0.789, -0.757/-0.790, -0.763/-0.757 and -0.770/-0.745 bar, whereas ST2-A/B changed -0.021/-0.003 bar. This connection-following pattern and its numerical match to the approximately -0.75-bar calibration offset beginning at 90 seconds support a shared measurement-path problem, not eight individual hardware diagnoses or a localized leak. Each affected tap had only 12/15 usable readings during 105-120 seconds, so missing portions remain unknown; the final five seconds nevertheless contained five usable readings per tap. During those final five seconds, 115-120 seconds, ST1-A/B were 0.772/0.759 bar below the supplied normal reference, versus ST2-A/B at 0.003 bar below and 0.014 bar above it, respectively, preserving the connection-specific contrast. Independent losses outside that connection during the recorded period would weaken the calibration-only interpretation.

P2-ST1-A/B changed from -0.029/-0.038 bar during 75-90 seconds to +0.353/+0.372 during 90-105 seconds and +0.356/+0.354 during 105-120 seconds, relative to first-60-second typical pressures. P2-ST8-A/B showed a smaller coherent rise of +0.267/+0.275 and +0.216/+0.234 bar in the last two periods, respectively; during the final five seconds, 115-120 seconds, ST1-A/B were 0.388/0.430 bar above normal and ST8-A/B 0.241/0.256 bar above normal. Direction and observed timing match the operating record's expected approximately +0.4-bar transition during 90-145 seconds, but the downstream magnitude is smaller and the recording ends at 120 seconds. Separately, P2-ST2-A's 81.773-bar peak and 2.934-bar adjacent step during the 0-120-second recording contrast with B's 79.324-bar maximum and 0.298-bar largest step, supporting a suspect excursion superimposed on the shared rise. P2-ST8-B is not demonstrated to be stuck: its profile changes with A despite a screening disagreement flag. Independent incident-period pressure/flow records could test exclusivity of the operating explanation; no supported joint leak pattern is established here.
